sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER LEVEL RIDGING WILL AMPLIFY ACROSS THE CENTRAL CONUS WHILE A STRONG UPPER LEVEL TROUGH REMAINS ANCHORED OVER THE WEST AND MAINTAINS MODEST DEEP-LAYER SWLY FLOW FROM SRN CA TO THE NRN ROCKIES AND ADJACENT HIGH PLAINS. IN THE EAST...A BROAD CYCLONIC CIRCULATION OFF THE SOUTHEAST COAST WILL REMAIN QUASI-STATIONARY WHILE STRONGER HEIGHT FALLS...ASSOCIATED WITH A DEEP LOW OVER THE NORTH ATLANTIC EAST OF NEWFOUNDLAND...WILL SPREAD ACROSS NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND. AT THE SURFACE...WEAK/RESIDUAL FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY TRAILS SWD FROM WI/IL THEN SWWD TO NEAR THE OK/KS BORDER AND THEN NWWD TO SERN CO. NUMEROUS OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES ARE ANALYZED ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE OLD FRONTAL ZONE...FROM IA/IL TO KS/OK/TX. DRY LINE IS BACKED WELL WEST INTO THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF NM AND SERN CO. BACKDOOR COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH THE NORTH ATLANTIC LOW IS CURRENTLY SITUATED ACROSS ERN QUEBEC AND THE GASPE PENINSULA.

sections.title: NEW ENGLAND/NY
sections.text: LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH LARGE SCALE HEIGHT FALLS AND BACKDOOR DOOR FRONT WILL ACT ON AN INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS ACROSS NRN NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON. WHILE STRONGEST INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED TO EXIST WELL AHEAD OF THE FRONTAL FORCING...FROM UPSTATE NEW YORK SWD...GREATEST CHANCE FOR STORM INITIATION BASED ON MOST MODEL GUIDANCE APPEARS TO BE OVER MAINE WHERE STRONGER FORCING AND WEAKER INHIBITION WILL COEXIST AMIDST SBCAPE OF 500-1000 J/KG. WEAK FRONTAL WAVE DEVELOPING ALONG THE ADVANCING FRONT MAY FURTHER AID STORM DEVELOPMENT/ORGANIZATION WHILE DEEP-LAYER FLOW/SHEAR STRENGTHENS TO GREATER THAN 40KT. A FEW FAST-MOVING AND SUSTAINED STORM UPDRAFTS MOVING SOUTH AT UP TO 40KT COULD PRODUCE LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL POSSIBLY AS LARGE AS GOLFBALLS. CHANCES FOR STRONG/SEVERE STORMS APPEAR TO BE LOWER WITH WWD EXTENT...ACROSS THE REST OF NRN NEW ENGLAND AND INTO ERN NEW YORK WHERE FORCING AND SHEAR WILL BE WEAKER. HOWEVER...SUBSTANTIAL INSTABILITY WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THESE AREAS WITH AN AXIS OF SBCAPE OF 2000-4000 J/KG FORECAST FROM THE ST. LAWRENCE VALLEY SEWD TO WRN MA AND NRN CT. FORECAST SOUNDING INDICATE LIMITED INHIBITION BY LATE AFTERNOON AND ALMOST ANY STORM INITIATING

sections.title: HIGH PLAINS/NM TO MT
sections.text: MID LEVEL SPEED MAX ROTATING THROUGH THE BASE OF LARGER SCALE TROUGH WILL SPREAD INLAND FROM SRN CA TO THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST THIS PERIOD. GRADUAL INCREASE IN THE SWLY MID LEVEL FLOW WILL COINCIDE WITH DIURNAL AND DIFFERENTIAL HEATING OVER THE FRONT RANGE AND ERN SLOPES OF THE ROCKIES WITH MOIST LOW LEVEL SELY UPSLOPE FLOW STRENGTHENING THROUGH THE DAY. BY 21Z...EXPECT SBCAPE VALUES TO RANGE FROM ABOUT 1000 J/KG OVER SERN MT TO AROUND 2000 J/KG ACROSS SERN NM. STORMS ARE LIKELY TO INITIATE ACROSS THIS ENTIRE EXTENSIVE REGION. STRONGER 0-6KM SHEAR OF 30-40KT IS FORECAST FROM CO TO WY WHERE A FEW TO SEVERAL SUPERCELLS COULD DEVELOP WITH ATTENDANT THREATS OF HAIL/WIND AND TORNADOES. INCREASING LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL DEVELOP ACROSS MT WHERE STORMS SPREADING OFF HIGHER TERRAIN MAY BE MAINTAINED WELL AFTER DARK...DEVELOPING EAST ALONG INSTABILITY GRADIENT FROM ERN MT INTO ND...IN THE FORM OF AN MCS WITH WIND AND HAIL. STORMS FROM SERN CO TO NM WILL ALSO POSE A THREAT OF SEVERE WIND/HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO BUT WILL EXIST IN SLIGHTLY WEAKER FLOW/SHEAR...COINCIDENT WITH LARGE SCALE HEIGHT RISES. THIS SUGGESTS THAT THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE PRIMARILY DIURNAL IN NATURE AND DECAY W

sections.title: TX
sections.text: HIGH RESOLUTION/STORM-SCALE GUIDANCE SUPPORTS THE POTENTIAL FOR ONE OR TWO CLUSTERS OF INTENSE CONVECTION TO DEVELOP WITHIN STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS OVER NW TX THIS AFTERNOON. OBSERVATIONAL EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THIS IS POSSIBILITY WITH A OUTFLOW/FRONT INTERSECTION AND WEAK MCV ASSOCIATED WITH DECAYING CONVECTION OVER THE PANHANDLE THIS MORNING. ABOUT 20KT 0-6KM SHEAR MAY PROMOTE SOME MULTICELL ORGANIZATION WITH STORM MERGERS AND OUTFLOW INTERSECTIONS PROVING TO BE AREAS WHERE DAMAGING WINDS AND SOME LARGE HAIL COULD OCCUR.

sections.title: KS/NEB TO UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: SIMILAR REGIME TO TX EXISTS NEAR THE RESIDUAL FRONTAL ZONE FROM KS/NEB TO IL/WI. MCV OVER NEB/KS ATTM MAY PROVIDE THE IMPETUS FOR MARGINALLY ORGANIZED STORMS...PERHAPS IN CLUSTERS OR BANDS...CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS SOME HAIL. ANOTHER CONCENTRATED AREA OF DEVELOPMENT IN WEAKLY SHEARED FLOW MAY EVOLVE ON THE WRN SHORE OF LAKE MI WHERE OLD FRONT WILL MERGE WITH LAKE BREEZE DURING PERIOD OF PEAK DESTABILIZATION.

sections.title: MO/OZARKS TO LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: VERY MOIST AIR MASS AND POCKETS OF STRONG HEATING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SBCAPE OF 1500-2000 J/KG FROM MO TO THE ARKLATEX AND LOWER MS VALLEY. WEAK INHIBITION WILL LEAD TO AN INCREASE IN PULSE STORMS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND INTO EARLY EVENING WITH A SCATTERING OF HAIL/WIND EVENTS POSSIBLE. ..CARBIN/ROGERS/GUYER.. 05/26/2010

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: A MOISTENING SELY FLOW REGIME IS NOW ESTABLISHED FROM ERN CO ACROSS ERN WY INTO SE MT. THE STRONGER INSTABILITY IS INITIALLY EXPECTED OVER CO WHERE BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS WILL RANGE FROM 56-60 F THIS AFTERNOON...WITH SOMEWHAT LESSER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE FARTHER NW INTO WY AND MT /DEWPOINTS OF 48-54 F/. THE INCREASING MOISTURE AND AFTERNOON TEMPERATURES WARMING INTO THE 70S /BENEATH 7 C/KM MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES/ WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES 1000-1500 J/KG. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY FORM BY MID AFTERNOON E OF THE MOUNTAINS FROM SE INTO NE CO...WITH DEVELOPMENT EXPECTED PROGRESSIVELY LATER IN THE AFTERNOON/EVENING FARTHER NW ACROSS WY INTO MT. THOUGH GRADUAL HEIGHT RISES ARE EXPECTED TODAY OVER THE HIGH PLAINS...THIS AREA WILL REMAIN WITHIN THE ENVELOPE OF 30-40 KT SWLY MID-UPPER FLOW...AND SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE WEAKER THAN PREVIOUS DAYS OVER ERN CO...BUT LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL BE ENHANCED SOME THIS AFTERNOON ALONG A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND TERRAIN-INDUCED CIRCULATION ACROSS SE CO. sections.title: NEW ENGLAND AREA THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO WARM WITH STRONG DAYTIME HEATING...WHILE A PLUME OF MID-UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS SPREADS SEWD FROM QUEBEC TO NY/NEW ENGLAND. THIS IS OCCURRING TO THE SW OF A COLD FRONT BACKING SWWD ACROSS MAINE...AND IN ADVANCE OF AN AMPLIFYING MIDLEVEL TROUGH APPROACHING NRN MAINE FROM THE MARITIME PROVINCES. THE NET RESULT THIS AFTERNOON WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODERATE INSTABILITY /MLCAPE OF 1500-2000 J PER KG/ IN AN ENVIRONMENT OF LARGELY UNIDIRECTIONAL 35-45 KT NNWLY FLOW. THERE ARE SOME CONCERNS REGARDING THE LACK OF A CLEAR FOCUS FOR STORM INITIATION...WITH THE SURFACE FRONT SOMEWHAT REMOVED FROM THE CORRIDOR OF STRONGER INSTABILITY. CURRENT EXPECTATIONS ARE FOR AT WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS TO FORM BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON OVER W/SW MAINE IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE FRONT...WITH MORE ISOLATED STORMS FARTHER TO THE W/SW ACROSS VT/NH/NE NY IN CONJUNCTION WITH LOCAL TERRAIN. ANY STORMS THAT FORM WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL THIS AFTERNOON INTO THIS EVENING.

sections.title: MS VALLEY REGION THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THE NET IMPACT OF CONVECTION OVER THE PAST TWO DAYS HAS BEEN TO REDUCE LAPSE RATES/INSTABILITY ACROSS THE MS VALLEY REGION. STILL...MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS SHOW THE POTENTIAL FOR MODERATE INSTABILITY AGAIN THIS AFTERNOON FROM ERN WI SWD ACROSS IL/MO/AR/LA. A FEW STORMS WITH STRONG DOWNBURST WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON. ..THOMPSON/HURLBUT.. 05/26/2010

sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE SRN...CENTRAL AND NRN HIGH PLAINS...

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: FORECAST APPEARS ON TRACK AS WARMING OF MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER HAS RESULT ALREADY RESULTED IN SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS TO DEVELOP ACROSS ERN CO...REFERENCE WW 223. OUTFLOW BOUNDARY MOVING WWD FROM WRN KS CONVECTION WILL AID MORE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS ERN CO/WRN KS...AND STORMS WILL EVENTUALLY DEVELOP ACROSS ERN WY AND SERN MT BY LATE AFTERNOON. HAIL STILL APPEARS TO BE THE MAIN THREAT...THOUGH AS MENTIONED IN PREVIOUS OUTLOOK... STRONGLY VEERING WINDS IN THE LOW LEVELS...COMBINED WITH RIGHT MOVING SUPERCELLS...WOULD RESULT IN FAVORABLE LOW LEVEL SRH FOR TORNADOES.

sections.title: NEW ENGLAND AREA
sections.text: NEARLY CLEAR SKIES HAS WARMED TEMPERATURES TO NEAR 90F AND WITH DEWPOINTS IN LOWER/MID 60S...RESULTING IN MLCAPES RANGING FROM 2500-3500 J/KG. THIS INSTABILITY ALONG WITH 30-35 KT DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS. HOWEVER...FORCING WILL BE WEAK SO STORM DEVELOPMENT IS IN QUESTION...REFERENCE 716 FOR MORE DETAILS.

sections.title: SRN PLAINS EWD INTO AR AND NEWD INTO IL
sections.text: UPPER RIDGE IS GENERALLY LOCATED OVER REGION AND IS RESULTING IN WEAK SHEAR. HOWEVER...STRONG HEATING OF MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM OVERNIGHT STORMS WILL RESULT IN NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS INTO THE EARLY EVENING HOURS. DESPITE THE WEAK SHEAR...MODERATE INSTABILITY...PW/S VALUES BETWEEN 1.25-1.50 INCHES AND PCPN LOADING COULD RESULT IN A FEW STORMS WITH MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL/STRONG WIND GUSTS. HOWEVER...THE SLOW MOTION OF STORMS AND MOIST ENVIRONMENT SUGGESTS LOCALIZED HEAVY RAINS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREAT. ..IMY.. 05/26/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1147 AM CDT WED MAY 26 2010/

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: IN MID-UPPER LEVELS...CONUS PORTION OF LARGE-SCALE PATTERN FEATURES MEAN TROUGHING OFF E AND W COASTS...AND HIGH-AMPLITUDE RIDGE FROM N-CENTRAL MEX/FAR W TX NNEWD ACROSS CENTRAL PLAINS THEN NEWD OVER UPPER GREAT LAKES. NET SHOREWARD MOTION IS FCST WITH LARGE CYCLONIC GYRE OFFSHORE PAC NW. MEANWHILE...SERIES OF LOWER-AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE PERTURBATIONS WILL TRAVERSE CYCLONIC FLOW BELT TO ITS E...FROM CENTRAL/SRN CA NEWD ACROSS NV THEN NNEWD OVER NRN ROCKIES. FARTHER E...WRN/TRAILING PORTION OF SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER ERN QUE IS FCST TO MOVE SWD ACROSS MAINE/NH OVERNIGHT...AS UPPER CYCLONE INITIALLY OVER FAR NWRN ATLANTIC RETROGRADES SWWD OVER NEWFOUNDLAND ISLAND. 23Z SFC ANALYSIS SHOWED RATHER NEBULOUS PATTERN WITH FORMERLY BETTER-DEFINED FRONTAL ZONE FROM UPPER GREAT LAKES TO S-CENTRAL PLAINS HAVING BEEN MODULATED BY NUMEROUS/INTERVENING OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES. DRYLINE WAS ANALYZED VERY CLOSE TO ERN RANGES OF ROCKIES FROM CO-MT. COMBINED FRONTAL-WAVE/LEE-SIDE CYCLONE WILL BECOME BETTER-DEFINED BY 12Z OVER SERN MT...WITH WARM FRONTOGENESIS OCCURRING SEWD ACROSS BLACK HILLS. SFC CYCLONE WAS ANALYZED OVER RI/SERN MA AREA INVOF INLAND-PENETRATING SEA BREEZE FRONT...WITH COLD FRONT NWWD ACROSS

sections.title: HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED SVR TSTMS -- INCLUDING A FEW SUPERCELLS WITH POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WIND AND SVR HAIL...ARE EXPECTED OVER THIS CORRIDOR FOR ANOTHER FEW HOURS. REF WWS 223-224 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST/NOWCAST INFORMATION ON SVR SITUATION IN AND NEAR THOSE AREAS FROM ERN MT TO ERN CO. INCREASING MLCINH SHOULD LEAD TO DECREASE IN TSTM COVERAGE/INTENSITY LATER THIS EVENING OVER CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...HOWEVER STG LOW-LEVEL WAA AND MOIST ADVECTION/TRANSPORT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO MORE PROLONGED CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL OVER PORTIONS ERN MT/WRN DAKOTAS DURING OVERNIGHT PERIOD. SVR POTENTIAL WITH LATTER ACTIVITY SHOULD DIMINISH WITH NEWD EXTENT AS INFLOW-LAYER PARCELS BECOME MORE ELEVATED AND MORE MARGINALLY BUOYANT.

sections.title: NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: ALB RAOB...AND CHH SOUNDING MODIFIED FOR SFC CONDITIONS W OF SEA BREEZE REGIME...INDICATE LOW-MIDLEVEL THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES AND DEEP-LAYER SHEAR FAVORABLE FOR LARGE HAIL AND STG-DAMAGING GUSTS. REF SPC WW 225 AND ACCOMPANYING MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR NEAR-TERM INFORMATION. NEAR AND AFTER SCHEDULED 06Z WW EXPIRATION...MODIFIED RAOBS AND MODEL SOUNDINGS SUGGEST SUFFICIENT LOW-LEVEL STABILIZATION TO CONTRIBUTE TO SIGNIFICANTLY LOWERED CONVECTIVE COVERAGE AND LESSENED SVR THREAT...ALTHOUGH SOME TSTM POTENTIAL MAY PERSIST FOR MUCH OF TONIGHT AHEAD OF AFOREMENTIONED MID-UPPER LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH.

sections.title: UPPER GREAT LAKES TO GULF COAST AND SRN PLAINS
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TO SCATTERED TSTMS...ALL EMBEDDED WITHIN WEAK FLOW ALOFT IN PROXIMITY TO UPPER RIDGE...HAVE BEEN FORCED BY DIURNAL HEATING AND LIFT ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES. OVERALL DECREASING TENDENCY...IN BOTH INTENSITY AND COVERAGE...IS EXPECTED THROUGH REMAINDER EVENING AS BOUNDARY LAYER DIABATICALLY COOLS...COVERAGE OF OUTFLOW AIR BECOMES MAXIMIZED...AND LIFT WEAKENS ALONG THOSE BOUNDARIES. ..EDWARDS.. 05/27/2010
